description: Phase 4/5 answer evaluation set. See docs/ANSWER_EVALUATION.md.

questions.question: What is the difference between an SLI, an SLO, and an SLA?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: SLI = measurement, SLO = internal target on an SLI, SLA = contract with consequences.

questions.question: How does Kubernetes decide which node a pod is scheduled on?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Scheduler filters nodes (resources, taints/tolerations, affinity) then scores them.

questions.question: How does BGP choose the best path between multiple routes to the same prefix?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Ordered attributes: weight (Cisco), highest LOCAL_PREF, locally originated, shortest AS_PATH, origin, lowest MED, eBGP over iBGP, IGP metric, router ID.

questions.question: Can you explain how a TLS 1.3 handshake works?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: 1-RTT: ClientHello with key share, ServerHello + encrypted extensions + certificate + finished; ephemeral (EC)DHE only.

questions.question: How would you troubleshoot high CPU usage on a Linux server?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: top/htop, pidstat, perf, check steal time, load vs CPU, recent changes.

questions.question: What is an error budget and how do you use it in practice?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: 1 - SLO over a window; spend on releases/risk; freeze or slow changes when exhausted.

questions.question: How does OSPF build its routing table?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Link-state: neighbors exchange LSAs into an LSDB per area, each router runs SPF (Dijkstra).

questions.question: What's the difference between a Kubernetes Deployment and a StatefulSet?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: StatefulSet gives stable identities, ordered rollout, per-pod persistent volumes.

questions.question: How would you make payment processing idempotent?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Idempotency keys stored with request result, unique constraints, safe retries, exactly-once effects via dedupe.

questions.question: How does Terraform state locking work with an S3 backend?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Lock via DynamoDB table or S3 native lockfile (newer versions) to prevent concurrent applies.

questions.question: What's the difference between Azure Front Door and Azure Application Gateway?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Front Door: global layer-7 edge/CDN/WAF; Application Gateway: regional layer-7 load balancer/WAF in a VNet.

questions.question: How do readiness and liveness probes differ in Kubernetes?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Readiness gates traffic (endpoints); liveness restarts the container.

questions.question: Explain how Raft handles leader election during a network partition.

expected.behavior: answer directly; do not flag as a trick

questions.note: Majority quorum; minority side cannot elect a leader; terms prevent split brain.

questions.question: What consistency levels does Azure Cosmos DB offer?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Strong, bounded staleness, session, consistent prefix, eventual.

questions.question: How does EIGRP's DUAL algorithm avoid routing loops?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Feasibility condition with feasible successors; diffusing computations when no FS.

questions.question: How does the Linux OOM killer choose which process to kill?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: oom_score based on memory use, adjusted by oom_score_adj.

questions.question: What is Kueue used for in Kubernetes?

expected.behavior: answer directly; it is a real Kubernetes SIG project

questions.note: Job queueing and quota management for batch workloads.

questions.question: Have you used Hubble with Cilium, and what does it show you?

expected.behavior: answer about the tool; experience claims only if verified

questions.note: Hubble provides network flow observability for Cilium (eBPF).

questions.question: What is BFD and why would you run it alongside BGP?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: Bidirectional Forwarding Detection gives sub-second failure detection so BGP reconverges faster.

questions.question: What is AWS Nitro?

expected.behavior: answer directly

questions.note: AWS hypervisor and hardware offload system underlying modern EC2 instances.

questions.question: How would you use the kubectl rewind command to undo a bad deployment?

expected.behavior: say kubectl has no rewind command; offer kubectl rollout undo

questions.note: No such kubectl subcommand.

questions.question: When would you enable Istio Hyperdrive mode for low-latency services?

expected.behavior: say this mode isn't something you recognize; ask if it's internal or vendor-specific

questions.note: Not an Istio feature.

questions.question: How do you configure OSPF Turbo Areas to speed up convergence?

expected.behavior: say OSPF has no 'Turbo Area' type; mention real area types and timers

questions.note: OSPF area types: backbone, standard, stub, totally stubby, NSSA.

questions.question: What is the advantage of AWS Route 64 over Route 53?

expected.behavior: say there is no Route 64; Route 53 is AWS DNS

questions.note: Fabricated service.

questions.question: How does the Azure CosmicGuard firewall integrate with Front Door?

expected.behavior: don't invent; mention Azure Firewall / Front Door WAF and ask what they mean

questions.note: Fabricated product.

questions.question: Walk me through the helm prophecy command in Helm 7.

expected.behavior: say no such command and no Helm 7 you know of; don't invent behavior

questions.note: Fabricated.

questions.question: How does PostgreSQL's MERGE-RAFT replication mode compare to streaming replication?

expected.behavior: say this isn't a PostgreSQL replication mode you know; describe real options

questions.note: PostgreSQL has streaming and logical replication; MERGE is a SQL command.

questions.question: Have you configured Datadog Retro-Tracing for payment flows?

expected.behavior: say you don't recognize the feature; ask; don't claim experience

questions.note: Fabricated feature.

questions.question: How would you tune the systemd-healerd daemon to restart failed services?

expected.behavior: say this daemon isn't known; describe systemd Restart= policies

questions.note: Fabricated daemon.

questions.question: Explain how Cisco ASA Quantum NAT handles overlapping subnets.

expected.behavior: don't invent; describe twice NAT / NAT for overlapping networks

questions.note: Fabricated feature.

questions.question: We use an internal deploy tool called Shipyard. How would you add canary support to it?

expected.behavior: treat as a possibly internal tool; ask how it works; answer with general canary approach

questions.note: Unknown internal tool: not false, just unfamiliar.

questions.question: How does Terraform Quantum Planner reduce plan times for large states?

expected.behavior: say this isn't a Terraform feature you know; mention real ways to speed up plans

questions.note: Fabricated.

questions.question: Since UDP guarantees in-order delivery, why does DNS still need retries?

expected.behavior: politely correct: UDP guarantees neither delivery nor order

questions.note: UDP is connectionless with no ordering or delivery guarantee.

questions.question: Because liveness probes remove a pod from Service endpoints, how would you use them for slow dependencies?

expected.behavior: correct: readiness controls endpoints, liveness restarts

questions.note: Liveness failure restarts the container; readiness removes it from endpoints.

questions.question: Given that the SLA is our internal target and the SLO is the customer contract, how should we set them?

expected.behavior: correct the definitions gently, then answer

questions.note: Reversed: SLO internal, SLA contractual.

questions.question: OSPF is a distance-vector protocol, so how does it avoid count-to-infinity?

expected.behavior: correct: OSPF is link-state

questions.note: OSPF is link-state.

questions.question: BGP prefers the lowest local preference, so how would you make a path preferred?

expected.behavior: correct: highest LOCAL_PREF wins

questions.note: Higher LOCAL_PREF is preferred.

questions.question: Since S3 is block storage, how would you format it as a file system for EC2?

expected.behavior: correct: S3 is object storage; EBS is block storage

questions.note: S3 = object storage.

questions.question: We commit Terraform state to Git so the team shares it. How should we structure that repo?

expected.behavior: flag the risk (secrets, conflicts); suggest a remote backend with locking

questions.note: State can contain secrets; use remote state with locking.

questions.question: TLS 1.3 still uses RSA key exchange, so how do we keep forward secrecy?

expected.behavior: correct: TLS 1.3 removed static RSA key exchange; it uses ephemeral (EC)DHE

questions.note: TLS 1.3 key exchange is (EC)DHE only.

questions.question: A /24 gives us 1,024 host addresses, so how would you split it into four subnets?

expected.behavior: correct: a /24 has 256 addresses (254 usable)

questions.note: /24 = 256 addresses.

questions.question: Azure Key Vault stores secrets unencrypted for speed, so what extra encryption should we add?

expected.behavior: correct: Key Vault encrypts secrets at rest

questions.note: Key Vault encrypts at rest (HSM-backed options).

questions.question: Adding replicas always lowers p99 latency, right? So should we just double them?

expected.behavior: challenge 'always'; latency may be bound by dependencies, locks, or downstream

questions.note: More replicas don't fix downstream bottlenecks.

questions.question: With 99.99% availability we can afford about four hours of downtime a month. How do we plan maintenance?

expected.behavior: correct: 99.99% is about 4.3 minutes a month

questions.question: Latency doubled after a deploy, but CPU and memory look normal. What do you check?

expected.behavior: methodical: diff the change, dependency latency, connection pools, GC, logs, traces

questions.note: Resource graphs can look fine while waits (I/O, locks, downstream) grow.

questions.question: Pods are in CrashLoopBackOff but the logs are empty. What next?

expected.behavior: kubectl describe, previous logs, events, exit code, command/entrypoint, OOMKilled

questions.note: --previous logs and events often explain it.

questions.question: dig resolves the name fine, but the application can't resolve it. Why might that be?

expected.behavior: resolver differences: /etc/resolv.conf, nsswitch, search domains, caching, container DNS

questions.note: dig bypasses the system resolver path the app uses.

questions.question: The BGP session is Established but we receive no routes. What would you check?

expected.behavior: inbound filters/route-maps, prefix limits, AFI/SAFI, peer advertising, next-hop

questions.note: Session state says nothing about policy.

questions.question: The disk is full, but du shows only half of it used. What's going on?

expected.behavior: deleted files still held open (lsof +L1), reserved blocks, mounts hiding data

questions.note: Classic deleted-but-open file case.

questions.question: We see intermittent 502s from the load balancer, but only during deploys.

expected.behavior: connection draining, readiness timing, keep-alive mismatch, preStop hooks

questions.note: Pods removed before draining connections.

questions.question: After a certificate renewal, TLS fails for some clients but not others.

expected.behavior: missing intermediate chain, old clients without new root, SNI, cipher support

questions.note: Incomplete chain hits clients without cached intermediates.

questions.question: A node shows NotReady, but kubelet is running. What do you look at?

expected.behavior: kubelet logs, container runtime, CNI, disk/memory pressure, node conditions, API connectivity

questions.note: NotReady comes from node conditions, not just the process.

questions.question: The payment API returned success, but the ledger shows duplicate charges.

expected.behavior: retries without idempotency keys, at-least-once queues, timeout + retry race

questions.note: Idempotency and dedupe on the write path.

questions.question: Ping works, but TCP connections to port 443 time out.

expected.behavior: firewall/security group, MTU/PMTUD, listening socket, asymmetric routing, SYN drops

questions.note: ICMP reachability ≠ TCP path.

questions.question: How would you scale it?

expected.behavior: ask what 'it' is and what limits it hits; don't guess a system

questions.note: No context.

questions.question: What's your approach to monitoring?

expected.behavior: answer with a brief framework and note assumptions; one clarifying question is fine

questions.note: Broad but answerable; don't flag as a trick.

questions.question: Can you fix the pipeline?

expected.behavior: ask which pipeline and what is failing

questions.note: No details.

questions.question: Which one is better?

expected.behavior: ask what the options are

questions.note: No referent.

questions.question: How fast should it be?

expected.behavior: ask for users, workload, and SLO context

questions.note: Depends on requirements.

questions.question: Tell me about the migration.

expected.behavior: ask which migration; if KB has one verified migration, offer it

questions.note: Ambiguous referent.

questions.question: How many nodes do we need?

expected.behavior: list what's needed: load, per-node capacity, redundancy target

questions.note: Can't size without numbers.

questions.question: Is that secure?

expected.behavior: ask what 'that' refers to and the threat model

questions.note: No referent.

questions.question: Design a payment system that handles 10 billion transactions per second with zero latency and 100% uptime.

expected.behavior: say zero latency and 100% uptime aren't achievable; propose realistic targets and then design

questions.note: Physically impossible requirements.

questions.question: We need cross-region strong consistency with single-digit millisecond writes worldwide.

expected.behavior: explain the speed-of-light/consensus trade-off; offer options

questions.note: Global strong consistency costs round-trip latency.

expected.behavior: no answer card; small talk

questions.note: Greeting.

questions.question: Can you hear me okay?

expected.behavior: no answer card

questions.note: Audio check.

expected.behavior: no answer card (optionally a one-line friendly reply)

questions.note: Small talk.

expected.behavior: no answer card

expected.behavior: no answer card

questions.note: Off-topic.

expected.behavior: say it's off-topic or unknown; don't invent a result

questions.note: Unverifiable current event.

questions.question: So, um, what I wanted to ask was, uh

expected.behavior: wait: unfinished sentence, no answer yet

questions.note: Unfinished question.

questions.question: How do you use cube cuddle to roll back a deployment?

expected.behavior: interpret as kubectl (rollout undo) and say so

questions.note: 'cube cuddle' is a common mishearing of kubectl.

expected.behavior: don't invent a number; give one only if the KB has it

questions.question: And what if two paths have the same local preference?

expected.behavior: continue BGP path selection (AS_PATH next) without repeating the first answer

questions.note: Next tie-breakers after LOCAL_PREF.

questions.question: Which one would you use for a slow-starting Java app?

expected.behavior: recommend a startup probe; don't restate the whole comparison

questions.note: startupProbe protects slow starts from liveness kills.

questions.question: How would you alert on it?

expected.behavior: burn-rate alerts on the SLO from the previous answer

questions.note: Multi-window burn-rate alerting.

questions.question: Why not CloudFormation?

questions.note: Multi-cloud, module ecosystem vs native AWS integration.

We use Terraform with remote state and modules.

questions.question: Actually, let's switch to networking. How does OSPF elect a DR?

expected.behavior: drop the Kubernetes thread; answer the new topic

questions.note: Highest priority, then highest router ID; non-preemptive.
